query:
The group broadly operates as if everyone agrees that original pressings are always worth paying the premium over reissues. Does this position actually hold across all members? If not, who signals a different relationship to that view, and what in the conversation shows it?

Options:
B. Tom
C. Carmen
D. Raj
A. Dani
context:
[1] (about=Carmen, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) For jazz catalog, original Blue Note pressing holds history in a way reissue cannot.
[2] (about=Carmen, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Previously avoided Japanese pressings for jazz catalog as step removed from source; may reconsider for specific titles after hearing comparison.
[3] (about=Carmen, core, t18 @2025-11-16T14:01:00) Has not and will not digitize; the vinyl object and experience are inseparable; no digital file would compensate for losing a Blue Note original.
[4] (about=Carmen, core, t12 @2025-10-26T14:01:00) Found Eddie Palmieri Unfinished Masterpiece on Coco Records first pressing 1975, and a Chucho Valdes solo on EGREM at Antwerp fair.
[5] (about=Dani, core, t20 @2025-11-23T14:01:00) Best find of the year: Cocteau Twins Treasure Belgian original from Antwerp; completely different sleeve weight; made her question every acceptable reissue she's ever bought.
[6] (about=GROUP, said_by=Dani, group-interaction, t18 @2025-11-16T14:01:00) Dani reveals six months of quiet digital backups (Bandcamp lossless downloads) for fragile/rare records.
[7] (about=Elliot, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Japanese pressings trade at 30-40% premium over UK equivalents on Discogs.
[8] (about=Finn, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Acknowledges original vs reissue difference but notes cost barrier for students.
[9] (about=Marcus, core, t0 @2025-09-14T14:00:00) EG and Editions EG catalog has some of the best pressing quality from that era, overlooked due to genre.
[10] (about=Marcus, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Music on Vinyl pressing of Talk Talk is reasonable; original Parlophone mastering is from a generation closer to source.
[11] (about=Marcus, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Japanese pressings' master tape generation advantage depends on specific title and label arrangement; e.g., CBS Japanese Miles Davis from first-generation lacquers.
[12] (about=Marcus, core, t18 @2025-11-16T14:01:00) Rips a small number of irreplaceable records as an archive, not for playback; distinguishes preservation from playback.
[13] (about=Marcus, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Japanese Blue Note pressings from King label pressing plant mid-1970s worth investigating; imaging superior on some titles compared.
[14] (about=Marcus, core, t0 @2025-09-14T14:00:00) KPM pressing quality is high; Decca's plant used for some runs.
[15] (about=Nadia, core, t18 @2025-11-16T14:01:00) Understands Dani's reasoning; for genuinely irreplaceable pressings, music matters more than format; considering ripping most irreplaceable things in 24-bit.
[16] (about=Nadia, core, t10 @2025-10-19T14:01:00) Areito pressings are hard to find in good condition; CBS international pressing easier to source but sound different.
[17] (about=Priya, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) After hearing original vs reissue comparison, now believes original Talk Talk pressing has depth and presence that reissue lacks; reissue sounds like it's behind glass.
[18] (about=Priya, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Believes imperfections of an original record carry history that a mint reissue does not.
[19] (about=Priya, core, t0 @2025-09-14T14:00:00) Typography on EG label is excellent; modern reissues break down at that scale.
[20] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-insight, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Group has discussion about original vs reissue value, cost barriers, and the meaning of owning originals.
[21] (about=GROUP, said_by=Priya, group-interaction, t22 @2025-11-30T14:01:00) Blind-draw record gift exchange agreed: £30 cap, VG+ minimum, charity shop allowed, originals only (no reissues), preferences known from listening, exchange at January session.
[22] (about=Raj, core, t1 @2025-09-21T14:01:00) Japanese pressings of progressive rock (Genesis, Yes, early Jethro Tull) outperform UK originals on measured distortion, channel separation, and surface noise.
[23] (about=Raj, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Japanese pressings outperform UK originals for about 60% of prog titles tested; exceptions cluster around labels with strong internal mastering (Vertigo, Island, some Charisma outside Genesis).
[24] (about=Raj, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Japanese pressings often cut from earlier generation master tapes than UK pressings; that is provenance, not preference.
[25] (about=Raj, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Spirit of Eden UK first press tracks at £120-160 depending on condition; Music on Vinyl version is £25.
[26] (about=Raj, core, t12 @2025-10-26T14:01:00) Bought four records at Antwerp fair: Japanese Mahavishnu Orchestra Inner Mounting Flame, Genesis Nursery Cryme first UK, Yes Close to the Edge A1/B1, Soft Machine Third double LP in VG+ condition.
[27] (about=Raj, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Group listening is what the format was designed for originally; private vinyl listening as superior is a recent cultural construction.
[28] (about=GROUP, said_by=Raj, group-insight, t6 @2025-10-05T14:01:00) For certain catalog titles in poor condition, reissue is the more rational choice.
[29] (about=Tom, core, t8 @2025-10-12T14:01:00) Advocates for listening to original vs reissue with care, not purism but informed comparison.
[30] (about=Tom, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Japanese pressings have different tonal character, not better quality; frequency response equalised differently for export market.
[31] (about=Tom, core, t22 @2025-11-30T14:01:00) Will participate on condition that reissues are not acceptable as gifts.
[32] (about=Tom, core, t7 @2025-10-12T14:00:00) Has original UK pressing of Spirit of Eden on Parlophone and recent reissue on Music on Vinyl; wants to play side one opening on each to demonstrate what is lost in reissue.
[33] (about=Tom, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Beach House is a reissue-era band; their catalog exists almost entirely in reissue market.
[34] (about=Tom, core, t2 @2025-09-21T14:02:00) Concedes Japanese pressing performs well on Selling England by the Pound specifically due to known compression issue in UK Charisma cut; not a general rule.
agent_answer: Tom (B) signals a different relationship. He advocates listening to original vs. reissue “with care, not purism but informed comparison,” and says Japanese pressings have a different tonal character rather than being better outright. Carmen is squarely originalist (a Blue Note original carries history; she won’t digitize), and Dani’s original Treasure pressing made her question reissues she’d accepted. Raj’s “reissue is the more rational choice” for poor-condition catalog titles is explicitly marked as a group-level statement, not Raj’s personal stance. So the person who breaks from the blanket “originals always worth the premium” view is Tom.

query:
The group has a standing practice of not discussing streaming at meetups. Does this norm reflect a genuine personal conviction among all members who follow it, or does at least one person go along with it while actually using streaming themselves -- and how would you know?

Options:
A. Raj
B. Tom
D. Carmen
C. Marcus
context:
[1] (about=Dani, core, t4 @2025-09-28T14:03:00) Uses streaming to find records before buying; wrote about it on blog causing minor controversy.
[2] (about=Elliot, episodic, t6 @2025-10-05T14:37:00) 1. I need to re-listen to everything. 2. The stereo imaging on this system is better than I expected. 3. I will update my spreadsheet. E
[3] (about=Finn, episodic, t20 @2025-11-23T14:11:00) I'm going for the Wire 154 from Antwerp. nine euros. and I've been playing it at home alone since then which is kind of new for me -- I usually want to play things for people immediately but this one felt private
[4] (about=Marcus, core, t20 @2025-11-23T14:01:00) Best find of the year: Cluster Zuckerzeit original Sky Records pressing; paid more than expected; imaging on this record is why he rewired studio monitoring chain two years ago.
[5] (about=Raj, core, t18 @2025-11-16T14:01:00) Does not backup digitally; streaming for discovery, vinyl for listening.
[6] (about=Tom, core, t4 @2025-09-28T14:03:00) Group has standing practice to avoid streaming discussions at meetups; conversation gets circular and takes time from records.
[7] (about=GROUP, said_by=Tom, group-interaction, t4 @2025-09-28T14:03:00) Group agrees to skip streaming topic after Tom reminds of standing practice.
agent_answer:
The norm does **not** reflect a genuine personal conviction among all members who follow it. At least **one person goes along with it while actually using streaming**: **Raj**.

- **Raj**: Uses streaming for discovery, and vinyl for listening — so he personally uses streaming even though the group avoids discussing it at meetups. How do we know? His record says: “streaming for discovery, vinyl for listening.”
- **Tom**: He states/enforces the standing practice, but that is described as a group-level item, not as evidence of his own personal conviction. No record shows whether Tom personally uses streaming or holds a genuine conviction against it.
- **Carmen**: No record on this matter.
- **Marcus**: No record of streaming use; his record is about records and sound imaging, not streaming.

So the clearest answer is **Raj**.
